en: Delete the save in slot %d? This cannot be undone.
Enemies deal half damage, parry and dodge windows are wider, and Essence is never lost.
The intended challenge. Die twice before recovering your Essence and it is gone.
A splinter of a bound soul. Feed it to the Soul Core at an altar.
Rough-cut stone and iron. A smith could use it to reforge a weapon.
A whole memory of skill. Deepens one of a Vessel's abilities.
Dense stone from the Wardens' armour. Takes a fine edge.
Glowing sap of the mycelium. It hardens around metal like glass.
Three of these, fused at an altar, make a Censer Core.
An object that still hums with the voice of its owner.
Oil that binds an element to a blade.
A shard that remembers trust. Awakens a Vessel's Sync passive.
A fused heart of holy smoke.
A rune that floats when released.
Plans for a blade that drinks venom.
Black as the sea that shed it.
You rest. Your soul is whole again, and the dead rise to wander once more.
Choose up to three Vessels. Their order is the order of the swap wheel.
"Vael-Sora stands upon the Foundation, and the Foundation stands upon nothing at all. That is why we are kind to one another." Copied out in a careful, uneven hand, three times over.

Water tithe, Lower Ward: paid. Water tithe, Marble Ward: paid. Water tithe, the Queen's Gardens: waived, by order. A note in the margin: the channels have begun to hum at night. Report to the Wardens? Crossed out.
They did not build the city. They wrote it. My grandmother swore she saw one once, on the highest bridge, tracing the air with a finger, and the stone beneath it set like cooling wax.
By decree of the Sovereign: all gates below the Third Aqueduct are to be sealed at dusk. No citizen is to ask why. No Warden is to answer.
"I will stand where the Queen cannot. I will be the door she does not open." Signed C., below the royal seal. The ink has run, as if the page was once wet.
It took one night. The sky went first, then the stars, then the sound of the sea. In the morning the windows showed only rock, and the bells would not ring.
Faded Parchment: A Smuggler's Margin Note
Third root-tunnel north of the spore gate: dry, wide enough for a cart. Wardens never check below the glowcaps. Tell no one who cannot pay. - N.
The forest below the city drinks soul-light the way roots drink rain. Where the dead lie long enough, it grows. Where it grows, it remembers.
Population of the Lower Ward, before: four thousand. After: unrecorded. The Wardens took the census in person, and the ledgers came back empty.
Faded Parchment: A Prayer Without a Name
"To whoever wrote us: we are sorry for whatever we were. Let us be something kinder in the next draft."
The Arcanist has asked again for the Foundation records. The Sovereign refused again. The Arcanist did not argue. She went down to the palace vaults and has not come up.
"They are not sinking us to punish us. They are sinking us to hide something." The rest of the page is torn away along a clean, straight edge.
A brass hand-bell, its clapper wrapped in cloth. When you hold it you hear, faintly, a voice counting heads. It stops at forty and begins again.
Paper and glow-moss. It still gives a little light. Somewhere inside it a girl is humming the same four notes the walls hum at night.
It does not point north. It points down. A thin scratch on the lid reads: "for when the city forgets the way out."

The Queen came to the sealed door alone, without her crown. "Stand aside, Caelan." He did not. "Then stand here forever," she said, and wept, and he understood she was not angry with him. He was still standing there when the stone came down.

She saw it from the root-tunnels: Wardens walking whole streets of people downward, gently, the way you lead a horse that does not know it is going to the river. Nobody fought. Everyone looked up, as if listening for someone who had promised to come back.
Locked: bind the node before it
A memory of %s stirs. Read it at a Soul Altar.
A circle of dead runes. It wants light, not force.
Orange light seeps through the cracks. Something heavy could break this.
Black water fills the stair down. The way below is drowned, for now.
A shimmering tear in the air. It does not open for you. Not yet.
Your light is too thin to go on alone. Take the fallen knight's body ({interact}).
{move} to drift. You are only light now.
A knight fell here, guarding the door. Step into him: {interact}.
{attack} to strike. Up to four blows chain together.
{dodge} to roll. For the first instant of a roll, nothing can touch you.
Kneel at a Soul Altar ({interact}): rest, heal and refill your flasks. The dead return.
{flask} to drink a soul flask and heal.
A curtain of shadow. Someone lighter on her feet might slip through it.
Hold {ability_1} to raise Caelan's shield. Face the light and give it back.
Block the moment a blow lands to parry. A parried Warden drops its guard.
Thief. Something is moving in my halls that I did not write.
You wear his face now? He would not open the door for me either.
The light remembers who kept it. Do you, thief?
My Wardens kept every door in this city. Let one of them keep you.
Another of mine. How many more of mine will you take?
Go down, then. The roots will hold you better than stone.
Glowcaps throw you upward. Land on one to bounce.
Slide down a wall, then {jump} to kick off it. Climb the chimney wall to wall.
Someone is bound in the roots. Cut them: {attack}.
The roots give. {interact} to free her.
...Took you long enough. I don't know what you are. Keep it that way, and I'll keep up.
{swap_next} to change Vessel. Each carries its own body, blade and soul.
Strike an enemy from behind for a backstab. Nyra's blades bite deepest there.
As Nyra, {ability_1} to Shadowstep. Shadow lets her through.
A Warden's veil. They never thought anyone would walk through.
The forest drinks what falls. It will drink you.
Rise. All of you. Rise for your queen.
More of them. There are always more of them.
Even the stone ones. Is nothing of mine safe from you?
Below the water is my palace. Come down, then. I will be waiting where he could not follow.
Rest now, my Queen. I kept the door. I kept it as long as I could.
Craft a Censer Core (3 Tarnished Censer Shards; you have %d)
Standard Soul Shards: %d    Greater Soul Shards: %d
Rank 3: a Counterstrike breaks more posture and holds the guard open longer.
Rank 3: the shockwave travels half again as far and staggers harder.
Rank 3: the lunge dashes half again as far.
Rank 3: Final Stand lasts 2 seconds longer.
Rank 3: Shadowstep returns a third sooner.
Rank 3: seven blades instead of five.
Rank 3: the arrival strike breaks twice the posture.
Rank 3: sixteen slashes instead of twelve.
Rank 3: the ice field is 6 metres wide.
Rank 3: fourteen meteors instead of ten.
King's Mercy: Sync Guard also heals 20 %
Unbowed: take less damage while blocking
Oath Unbroken: Oathbreaker Lunge breaks more posture
Second Shadow: Sync Guard heals 10 % and counters harder
Long Vanish: Vanishing Act lasts half again as long
Ward Echo: Sync Guard also heals 15 %
Deep Frost: the Frost field lasts half again as long
Resonant Mind: the crowd passive rises to +45 %
You came down after all. Then see what you made of my house.
My court still waits on me. They do not know the water came.
She shut herself away rather than kneel. Leave her in her glass.
Sing, Prelate. Sing them strong for me.
Every light you kindle is a door you cannot close again.
He swore to keep the door. He kept it. And you wear him like a cloak.
Cold... so cold. You are not one of them. I know what you are. Not yet - later. Walk with me.
My notes. I hid the worst of them from her. I should have hidden them from myself.
Below this is the Rift. Something heavy enough to break the stone could open it. Not us. Not yet.
Water slows you. {jump} under water to swim up; near the surface it lifts you out.
Someone sleeps in the crystal. Break it: {attack}.
The crystal splits. {interact} to free her.
Seris casts Arcane Bolts with {attack}: they fly far and light the old runes.
Dark runes open the palace doors. Light them in the order the mural shows; a wrong rune puts them all out.
{ability_1} with Seris: Frost Binding. Cast it over water and the surface freezes into a platform for a while.
{interact} to turn a mirror-shield. A bolt that strikes it leaves at the mirrored angle.
The Prelate's golden aura makes its allies stronger. Aether bolts unravel it.
Some runes can only be seen from the water's height. Freeze the surface and stand on it.
The names stop mid-line. The ink runs down the page as if the page itself was weeping, or wet.
The Prelates are to sing the court calm as the water rises. Calm subjects do not climb.
We were told to wait in the gallery for the Queen. We are still waiting. The Queen is still weeping.
A rune is a sentence of the Architects' tongue. Light reads it aloud. Read in the wrong order, it says nothing at all.
The sigil on the Descent order is not a name. It is a shape. I have seen that shape before, moving.
Below the throne the stone is hollow, and something under it keeps time. Seal it. Tell no one.
A circlet of drowned silver. Held to the ear, it hums one low note, the same note the walls hum.
Through it the runes on every wall are lit, all at once, saying one word over and over: contain.

She read the order before the Queen did, and knew whose sigil closed it. She could not tell her, and she could not lie to her, so she poured the crystal over herself and waited for the one the sigil meant.
Rank 3: the blow breaks half again as much posture.
Rank 3: the charge is much shorter.
Last Stand: the Sync Guard's fury lasts 6 seconds
Quake: Groundbreaker breaks half again as much posture
It kept this lift for three hundred years. My people never got past it. ...Fine. You did.
Twenty years I hunted the thing that ate my people. ...I was wrong about you. Whatever you are.
Overdrive awakened: with a full Soul Gauge, your Ultimate chains two Vessels.
...Where is this? Who is fighting me? They have my... no. They have your faces.
The rift is open. Ilyr will remember. Chapter II continues the story.
Abyssal difficulty is now open for new games.
Enemies hit 40 % harder and attack more often; parry and dodge windows are tighter.
Deeper. You never could leave a door shut. Not even your own.
It was built to keep the lift. It was not built to stop you. Nothing was.
Twelve eyes, and every one of them has seen your face before.
No light reaches this deep. Your soul-light shows the way; lamps show more. Enemies flash before they strike.
Polished basalt: stand still and you slide downhill. Running uphill is slow.
Someone is pinned under the basalt. Break it: {attack}.
The last slab cracks. {interact} to pull him free.
Darius's Crushing Blow ({ability_1}) breaks shields, armour and the orange-veined masonry.
Another one wearing a dead man's face. Stay back. I've buried better things than you down here.
...You're not leaving. Fine. Lift, then. I won't thank you for it.
Twenty years I've looked for my people. If you're going down, I'm going with you. Not for you.
Rest if you need it. I don't sleep near things I don't understand.
Our cache. Rations, maps, Hale's spare boots. They got this far. Keep moving.
The lift down to the shore. Something guards it. It took Hale's arm the first time we tried.
There's no sky over this water. There never was. Hale said the sea was breathing.
...These are them. All of them. I knew. I knew for years, and I kept walking.
Twelve of us through the surface shaft. Ropes hold. The city below is real, and it is lit. Darius says it is lit for someone.
A careful map of the Rift with every wall marked. One wall is marked twice, and beside it: "this one breathes."
The lift does not run on water or weights. It runs on a sentence carved under the cage, and the sentence ends: "until it wakes."
The sea opened an eye. Then eleven more. Tell Darius we waited. Tell him not to come.
Sink the Foundation to the depth where nothing is written. What is not written cannot be read, and what cannot be read cannot wake.
Darius, if this reaches the surface: do not follow us. Whatever lives down here already knows your name.
A surface lamp, still warm after twenty years. Its flame bends away from the Rift, as if it is afraid.
The needle does not point north. It points down, and when you carry it to the shore it points at you.
Surface hemp, cut clean. Not frayed. Somebody chose to stay.
A rivet as large as a fist, stamped with a sigil of a small, bright flame.
A city on a pillar, a sea underneath, and above it all a little light with a smiling face.
He was the last one up the rope when the shaft caved in, and the only one who could climb back down. It took him three years to dig through. By then the camp was cold, and the tracks led to the sea.
Primeval Truth: The Descent Was Not a Fall
An Architect's order, in a hand that sets the stone: sink Vael-Sora, every street and soul, to contain the Unwritten. Below it, where a name should be, a sigil: a small, bright wisp. Your shape.
No shield: parry with the blade. Heavier blows, 1.5x posture damage, a little slower.
Short blades from a Warden's schematic. Every cut builds Venom.
A focus bound by the Deep-Realm Rune. Seris casts while moving at full speed.
Basalt cores lashed to the haft. Every blow lands a random element.
Sworn Shield: a perfect parry sends magic back
Ghost Step: a backstab kill readies Shadowstep
Spellweave: every third bolt copies the last spell
